items.title: Drone strike reported at Sana Elementary School in Amhara
items.text: Addis Standard reported that a strike hit the school on the morning of 20 October. Preliminary reports said at least six schoolchildren were killed and more than 20 injured. Other unverified accounts gave higher figures. The military did not respond to requests for comment.

items.title: Federal forces clash with armed groups in Adigrat
items.text: AFP reported that federal forces clashed with armed groups opposed to the government in Adigrat on October 17. Residents described burnt-out trucks in the city centre after earlier drone strikes on Eritrean troops.

items.title: Drone strikes reported around Rama
items.text: ACLED reported Ethiopian army drone strikes on Tigrayan force vehicles around Rama on 15 October, after similar strikes the day before. Reuters photos showed damaged homes; no casualty figures were independently confirmed.

items.title: Tigrayan forces claim to retake Abiy Addi
items.text: Tigray Defense Forces said they attacked government forces and took Abiy Addi, Shewate Higum and Yechila. A Tigray Peace Force commander had earlier said government-allied forces held the town. Neither claim was independently verified.

items.title: Ethiopian forces and allied fighters reported entering Axum
items.text: Ethiopian forces and allied Tigray Peace Force fighters said they entered Axum. ACLED documented the entry and said rival Tigrayan fighters stayed in surrounding areas. The entry date and any fighting there are not independently verified.

items.title: Hospital in Adwa reported looted
items.text: UN spokespeople said a hospital in Adwa was looted on Monday, and that looting of other public buildings was also reported in Tigray.

items.title: Ethiopian troops reported entering Zalambessa on Eritrean border
items.text: People in touch with residents told Reuters that Ethiopian government troops advanced into Zalambessa, which Tigrayan rebels had held. A pro-government militia spokesperson did not confirm army control. Eritrea denies sending troops into the area.

items.title: Government forces enter Adwa; looting reported
items.text: Residents told AFP that federal forces and allied fighters entered Adwa without resistance after TPLF-loyal forces withdrew. Residents said government buildings, including Adwa Hospital, were looted overnight.

items.title: Rival forces claim Adigrat
items.text: The Tigray Peace Forces said they control Adigrat. Reuters, citing three residents, said government forces and allied militia entered the city. Reuters could not confirm who controls it.

items.title: Drone strikes reported on Eritrean forces near Adigrat
items.text: The conflict monitor ACLED said multiple drone strikes hit Eritrean troops and ammunition in the Adigrat area overnight. Witnesses told AFP they saw destroyed Eritrean lorries and a large explosion. No casualty figures were reported.

items.title: Drone strikes reported on homes in Adwa
items.text: A situation report by the Europe External Programme with Africa, republished by IDN-InDepthNews, said drone strikes reportedly hit civilian homes in Adwa. The report says the information comes from third parties and is not verified.

items.title: Looting and gunfire reported in Shire after rebels leave
items.text: An aid worker told AFP that TPLF fighters and the local administration left Shire on Wednesday. AFP reported that looting followed and four people were killed and 11 injured in gunfire. Pro-government forces had not yet entered the city.

items.title: Federal forces reported to take control of Wukro
items.text: The Critical Threats Project reported that federal forces and the Tigray Peace Force paused outside Wukro from 5 October and took control of the town on 7 October.

items.title: Drone strike reported on Sheraro displacement camp
items.text: An aid worker told AFP that a drone strike early on Sunday on a camp for displaced people killed at least eight people, including a child, and seriously wounded six. AFP said it could not verify the toll independently.

items.title: Federal and allied forces say they took Mekelle
items.text: Residents told Xinhua that federal forces and the Tigray Peace Force took control of Mekelle late on Saturday, with limited fighting in or around the city.

items.title: Government forces retake Mekelle's airport
items.text: Ethiopian government forces recaptured Alula Aba Nega Airport after fighting that began on 23 September.

items.title: Drone strikes reported on hotels in Adwa
items.text: Residents told Addis Standard that drone strikes hit several hotels. One resident estimated up to nine civilians were killed. Addis Standard could not verify the figure, and no one has claimed the strikes.

items.title: Heavy fighting around Alamata
items.text: Government troops took control of Alamata after days of fighting. A medic told the BBC that at least 52 civilians were killed.

items.title: Drone strike hits Tigrai TV headquarters
items.text: A drone struck the building of Tigray's public television station in Mekelle, taking it off air. No casualties were reported at the time.

items.title: Mortar strike kills civilians in Kobo
items.text: The UN human rights chief reported that a mortar strike killed civilians in Kobo, in Amhara near the Tigray border.

items.title: Tigrayan forces capture Abala
items.text: Tigrayan forces captured Abala, a district capital in the neighbouring Afar region, as fighting spread.

items.title: Airports at Mekelle, Axum and Shire seized
items.text: Tigrayan forces seized the airports of Mekelle, Axum and Shire, and flights to the region were cancelled.

items.title: Airports at Mekelle, Axum and Shire seized
items.text: Tigrayan forces seized the airports of Mekelle, Axum and Shire, and flights to the region were cancelled.

items.title: Drone strike destroys food aid truck
items.text: A drone struck a truck carrying about 41 tonnes of food for displaced families in Sheraro. A 13-year-old girl was injured.

items.title: Drone strikes reported near Freweyni
items.text: Hintalo district officials told Tigray TV that drone strikes on a residential area in the MyShumet area near Freweyni killed three people, including a two-year-old child, and injured four. Addis Standard could not verify the figures. The federal government made no immediate comment.

items.title: Airstrike on a residential compound in Mekelle
items.text: Human Rights Watch found that an apparent Ethiopian government airstrike hit a compound for teachers and their families, wounding 13 civilians including 7 children.
